_comentario: Historias cortas con preguntas y retell (etapa 4). Tandas de 3 a 12; el retell NO es opcional. Las escribe Cowork; se anexan con tools/content/anexar_historias.py.

historias.title: An Early Saturday
text: Diego gets up at six every morning.
He takes a shower and drinks a cup of coffee.
He puts on his blue shirt and black shoes.
At seven o'clock he is at the bus stop.
Today the street is very quiet.
There are no cars and no people.
Diego looks at his cell phone.
It is Saturday, not Monday!
He goes home and goes back to bed.

preguntas.q: What time does Diego get up?
Why is the street quiet?
What does Diego do at the end?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en presente, con la -s de he/she (gets, takes, goes).
pistas: Diego gets up at six · a shower · coffee
at seven · the bus stop · very quiet
his cell phone · Saturday · back to bed

historias.trap: Con he/she el verbo lleva -s: 'he gets up', 'he takes', 'he goes'. El error típico es decir 'he get up' o 'he go home'.

historias.title: A Busy Monday
text: Rosa works in an office downtown.
Today is Monday, and the office is very busy.
Her boss is talking on the phone.
Two coworkers are eating lunch at their desks.
The printer isn't working again.
Rosa is writing emails and answering calls.
At five o'clock, her boss comes to her desk.
"Rosa, why are you here today?" he asks.
"Your vacation starts today!"

preguntas.q: Where does Rosa work?
What is not working?
Why is the boss surprised?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en presente. Usa el presente continuo (is talking, are eating) para lo que pasa en la oficina.
pistas: Rosa works · downtown · Monday
her boss is talking · coworkers are eating · the printer
at five · why are you here · vacation

historias.trap: El presente continuo necesita 'is/are': 'her boss is talking', no 'her boss talking'. Y en inglés se dice 'on the phone', no 'in the phone'.

historias.title: Salsa Upstairs
historias.titleEs: Salsa en el piso de arriba
text: Pedro and his wife have a new apartment.
It is small, but it is near a park.
There is a kitchen, a bathroom, and one bedroom.
There are two big windows in the living room.
The rent is only seven hundred dollars a month.
But every night at ten, there is a lot of noise upstairs.
Someone is dancing salsa.
It is his wife's mother!
She lives upstairs, and the building is hers.

preguntas.q: How many bedrooms are there?
What is the problem with the apartment?
options: It is far from the park

preguntas.q: Why is the rent probably cheap?
options: The owner is his wife's mother
preguntas.answer: The owner is his wife's mother

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en presente. Describe el apartamento con 'there is' y 'there are'.
pistas: Pedro and his wife · a new apartment · near a park
there is a kitchen · there are two windows · the rent
every night at ten · dancing salsa · his wife's mother

historias.trap: 'Hay' se dice 'there is' (una cosa) o 'there are' (varias). No se dice 'have a kitchen' ni 'there have'.

historias.title: Spanish in Chicago
text: Carla is on vacation in Chicago.
She is sitting in a small coffee shop downtown.
A coffee is two dollars, and a cookie is one.
The man next to her is talking on the phone.
He is speaking Spanish, very loudly.
He says the coffee here is terrible.
The woman behind the counter is smiling.
She answers him in perfect Spanish.
She is from Colombia, and the coffee shop is hers.

preguntas.q: How much is a coffee?
What does the man say about the coffee?
Why is the woman smiling?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en presente (is sitting, is talking, says).
pistas: Carla · Chicago · a small coffee shop
a coffee is two dollars · a man is talking on the phone
the coffee is terrible · the woman · from Colombia

historias.trap: 'Dollars' siempre lleva -s cuando son dos o más: 'two dollars', no 'two dollar'. Y el precio se dice con 'is': 'a coffee is two dollars'.

historias.title: Left, Then Right
text: Yesterday was cold and very windy.
Luis went downtown to meet his sister for lunch.
The restaurant was on Oak Street, but he was lost.
He saw a woman and asked for help.
"Turn left, then right, then left again," she said.
Luis went left, then right, then left again.
After twenty minutes, he was at the same corner.
The restaurant was right behind him!
His sister was at the window, laughing.

preguntas.q: How was the weather?
Who did Luis ask for help?
Where was the restaurant?
options: Behind him, at the same corner
preguntas.answer: Behind him, at the same corner

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado: was, were, went, saw.
pistas: yesterday · cold and windy · Luis went downtown
Oak Street · he was lost · he saw a woman
twenty minutes · the same corner · his sister was laughing

historias.trap: En pasado 'go' es 'went' (no 'goed') y 'see' es 'saw'. Con he/she/it se usa 'was': 'he was lost', 'the restaurant was behind him'.

historias.title: Three Cakes
text: Last Saturday was my grandmother's birthday.
There were fourteen people at her house.
My mother made a big chocolate cake.
My aunt made a chocolate cake too.
My cousin bought a cake at the store.
It was chocolate, of course.
There were three cakes, but there was no dinner.
My grandmother saw the cakes and laughed.
Then she went to the kitchen.
She had rice and chicken for everyone.

preguntas.q: How many people were at the house?
What kind of cakes were there?
What did the grandmother have in the kitchen?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado: was, were, made, bought, saw, went.
pistas: last Saturday · my grandmother's birthday · fourteen people
my mother made · my aunt made · my cousin bought
three cakes · no dinner · rice and chicken

historias.trap: Ojo: 'fourteen' (14) se acentúa al final, «for-TÍIN», y 'forty' (40) al principio, «FÓR-ti». Si los confundes, cambias el número.

historias.title: The Last Bus
text: Miguel finished work at eleven at night.
He walked to the bus stop and waited.
The last bus was at eleven fifteen, and it never came.
He was tired and it was starting to rain.
Then a car stopped next to him.
It was his neighbor, coming back from the airport.
She drove him home and they talked the whole way.
They lived on the same street for six years and never spoke to each other.

preguntas.q: Why didn't Miguel take the bus?
Who stopped the car?
What is surprising at the end?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia con tus palabras, en pasado.
pistas: Miguel · eleven at night · the bus
it was starting to rain · a car stopped
his neighbor · they talked

historias.trap: Ojo con 'waited': se escribe con -ed pero suena «WEI-tid», con sílaba aparte, porque wait termina en t.

historias.title: The Wrong Coffee
text: Every morning Ana orders the same coffee before work.
Last Tuesday the barista was new and got it wrong.
Ana didn't say anything because there was a long line behind her.
She drank it at her desk and it was terrible.
The next day the same barista saw her and smiled.
"Black coffee, no sugar, right?" he said.
He remembered her order from the day before.
Ana didn't have the heart to tell him it was wrong.

preguntas.q: What happened on Tuesday?
Why didn't Ana complain?
What did the barista remember?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta qué pasó los dos días.
pistas: every morning · the same coffee
Tuesday · the new barista
the next day · he remembered

historias.trap: 'Line' es la fila de gente. No es 'tail' ni 'row'. En inglés británico dicen 'queue'.

historias.title: Two Suitcases
text: When Carlos moved to another city, he took two suitcases.
He used to have a lot of things, but he sold most of them.
His friends told him he was crazy.
The first month was hard and the apartment felt empty.
After a while he stopped noticing.
Now, three years later, he still has almost nothing.
He says it is the best decision he ever made.

preguntas.q: How many suitcases did Carlos take?
What did he do with his things?
options: He gave them to his friends

preguntas.q: How does he feel now?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta qué hizo Carlos y qué piensa ahora.
pistas: he moved · two suitcases
he used to have · he sold
three years later · the best decision

historias.trap: 'Used to have' es lo que tenía antes y ya no. No es 'I was having'.

historias.title: The Dog That Waited
text: There is a small park near my office.
Every day at one o'clock a brown dog sits at the gate.
He doesn't bark and he doesn't move.
For weeks I thought he was lost.
Then one afternoon an old man arrived on a bicycle.
The dog ran to him and they left together.
Now I see them every day, always at the same time.

preguntas.q: Where does the dog sit?
options: At the gate of the park
preguntas.answer: At the gate of the park

preguntas.q: What did the narrator think at first?
Who came on a bicycle?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta lo que pasa cada día en el parque y qué descubriste un día.
pistas: a small park · one o'clock
a brown dog · he sits and doesn't bark
an old man · a bicycle

historias.trap: Presente simple para lo que pasa siempre: 'he doesn't bark', con doesn't y el verbo pelado.

historias.title: A Very Long Meeting
text: The meeting started at nine and it was going to last one hour.
At eleven, nobody could agree on anything.
People were checking their phones under the table.
Then the newest person in the team raised her hand.
"Can I ask what we are deciding?" she said.
Nobody answered for several seconds.
The meeting finished four minutes later.

preguntas.q: How long was the meeting going to be?
What were people doing under the table?
What happened just before the meeting finished?
options: A question from the newest person
preguntas.answer: A question from the newest person

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta cómo fue la reunión y cómo terminó.
pistas: it started at nine · one hour
at eleven · nobody could agree
the newest person · "what are we deciding?"

historias.trap: 'Last' aquí es el verbo durar, no 'último'. Es la misma palabra con dos significados.

historias.title: Rain in December
text: Last December we went to the coast for a week.
It rained every single day.
We couldn't swim and we couldn't walk on the beach.
On the fourth day we found a small place that sold soup.
We went back every afternoon after that.
The owner learned our names and kept a table for us.
We still talk about that trip more than the sunny ones.

preguntas.q: What was the weather like?
What did they find on the fourth day?
How do they talk about the trip now?
options: They talk about it more than the sunny trips
preguntas.answer: They talk about it more than the sunny trips

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta el viaje: cómo empezó y por qué lo recuerdan.
pistas: last December · the coast
it rained · we couldn't swim
a small place · soup · every afternoon

historias.trap: 'Couldn't' + verbo pelado: 'we couldn't swim', nunca 'we couldn't to swim'.

historias.title: The Song on Hold
text: Paula called her bank because her new card wasn't working.
A recorded voice said, "Please wait. Your call is important to us."
She waited for twenty minutes, and the same song played again and again.
While she was waiting, she was washing the dishes and singing along.
Suddenly a man said, "Hello?" but Paula was still singing loudly.
She was so embarrassed that she hung up the phone.
So she had to call back and wait again.
After forty minutes, the same man answered her call.
"Oh, it's the singer," he said. "How can I help you today?"

glosario.es: cantando al mismo tiempo (con la música)

preguntas.q: Why did Paula call the bank?
What was Paula doing while she was waiting?
Why did Paula hang up the first time?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado; usa el pasado continuo para lo que Paula estaba haciendo (was waiting, was singing).
pistas: Paula · the bank · her new card
while she was waiting · the dishes · singing
she hung up · forty minutes · the singer

historias.trap: 'Embarrassed' significa «avergonzada», no «embarazada» (eso es 'pregnant'). Es un falso amigo clásico.

historias.title: The Wrong Glasses
text: On Friday, Rodrigo went to the doctor with a bad headache.
"How long have you had it?" the doctor asked.
"Since last Monday," Rodrigo answered.
She checked his eyes and said they were fine.
"You should drink more water and sleep more," she said.
Then she looked at his glasses and started to laugh.
They weren't his glasses. They were his wife's glasses!
He took the wrong pair by mistake last Monday morning.
And his wife? She had a headache all week too.

preguntas.q: When did Rodrigo's headache start?
What did the doctor tell him to do?
options: Drink more water and sleep more
preguntas.answer: Drink more water and sleep more

preguntas.q: What was the real cause of his headache?
options: He was wearing his wife's glasses
He had a problem with his eyes
preguntas.answer: He was wearing his wife's glasses

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado; usa el present perfect en la pregunta del doctor («How long have you had it?») y 'should'.
pistas: Friday · the doctor · a bad headache · since last Monday
his eyes were fine · you should drink more water
she started to laugh · his wife's glasses · a headache too

historias.trap: No digas «I have a headache since Monday»: en inglés es 'I have had… since Monday'. Y 'since' va con un momento (Monday); 'for' con una duración (for five days).

historias.title: The Man in the Elevator
text: Valentina had a job interview at ten, and she was nervous.
In the elevator, she was practicing her answers out loud.
A man in a gray suit was standing next to her.
"You speak too fast," he said. "You should slow down a little."
She felt a bit annoyed, but she thanked him anyway.
Five minutes later, she walked into the interview room.
The man in the gray suit was sitting behind the desk.
"Let's start," he said with a smile. "Slowly this time, please."
She got the job, and he still reminds her to slow down.

preguntas.q: What was Valentina doing in the elevator?
What advice did the man give her?
Who was the man in the gray suit?
options: Another person looking for a job

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado; usa el pasado continuo (was practicing, was standing, was sitting) y 'should'.
pistas: Valentina · a job interview · the elevator
a man in a gray suit · you should slow down
behind the desk · she got the job

historias.trap: Después de 'should' va el verbo sin 'to': 'You should slow down', no «You should to slow down».

historias.title: The Borrowed Drill
text: In March, Ernesto lent his drill to his neighbor, Samuel.
Samuel needed it to put up some shelves in his living room.
"I'm going to give it back on Monday," he said.
Months passed, and Ernesto never saw the drill again.
Every time he saw Samuel, he wanted to ask, but he felt too shy.
Last Saturday he finally knocked on Samuel's door.
"I gave it back in April," Samuel said, surprised.
"Your wife was working in the yard, so I gave it to her."
Ernesto went home and asked his wife about it.
"Oh, yes," she said. "I've used it three times since then."

preguntas.q: Why did Samuel need the drill?
What did Samuel say last Saturday?
options: He gave it back in April
He was going to return it soon
preguntas.answer: He gave it back in April

preguntas.q: Who had the drill after April?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado y termina con lo que dijo la esposa en present perfect (I've used it…).
pistas: in March · lent his drill · shelves
months passed · too shy to ask
I gave it back in April · his wife

historias.trap: 'Lend' es prestar (dar) y 'borrow' es pedir prestado (recibir): «Can I borrow your drill?», no «Can you borrow me your drill?».

historias.title: Four Strangers and a Car
text: Lina was going to fly to Santa Marta for her best friend's wedding.
She was waiting at the gate when the airline canceled the flight.
The next flight with free seats was two days later, after the wedding.
She wasn't able to find a bus, so she decided to rent a car.
Three other people from the canceled flight asked to go with her.
They drove all night and took turns at the wheel.
They talked about their jobs, their families, and their favorite music.
In the morning, Lina asked, "Where should I take you?"
All three of them gave her the address of the wedding.

preguntas.q: Why was Lina traveling to Santa Marta?
Why didn't Lina wait for the next flight?
What was the surprise in the morning?
options: They were all going to the same wedding
They were all from the same town
preguntas.answer: They were all going to the same wedding

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta el viaje en pasado; usa 'was going to', 'was waiting' y 'wasn't able to'.
pistas: Lina · a wedding · the airline canceled the flight
rent a car · three other people · all night
where should I take you · the same address

historias.trap: En inglés americano se escribe 'canceled' con una sola l, y la -ed suena como una d suave: «CAN-suld», no «can-se-led».

historias.title: The Store on the Corner
text: When I was a kid, I used to ride my bike downtown.
There were very few cars, and the streets were much quieter.
My father used to buy the newspaper at a small store on the corner.
I have lived in another country for fifteen years.
Last month I went back, and I couldn't recognize my old street.
Now there are tall buildings, and the traffic is much worse.
The small store has become a big, modern coffee shop.
I went in, and the old owner was still behind the counter.
"I've been here since nineteen eighty," he said. "Only the coffee is new."

preguntas.q: What did the narrator use to do as a kid?
How long has the narrator lived in another country?
What was the surprise in the coffee shop?
options: The old owner was still there
preguntas.answer: The old owner was still there

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta cómo era la ciudad antes con 'used to' y cómo es ahora; usa 'for' y 'since'.
pistas: when I was a kid · I used to · the store on the corner
fifteen years · I couldn't recognize · tall buildings
a coffee shop · the old owner · since nineteen eighty

historias.trap: 'Used to' se pronuncia «IUS-tu», con s sorda y sin sonar la d; y solo habla del pasado: para el presente se dice 'I usually…', no «I use to…».

historias.title: The Email He Didn't Send
text: Andrés had been working at the company for eight years.
One Friday his manager took credit for a project he had finished alone.
That night he wrote a long email explaining everything.
He read it four times and then saved it as a draft.
On Monday he asked for a meeting instead.
The conversation lasted twenty minutes and it was uncomfortable.
But his name appeared on the project the following week.
He says the email would have felt better and worked worse.

preguntas.q: What had Andrés done?
What did he do with the email?
options: He saved it as a draft
preguntas.answer: He saved it as a draft

preguntas.q: What does he think now?
options: The meeting worked better than the email would have
preguntas.answer: The meeting worked better than the email would have

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta qué pasó y por qué él cree que hizo bien.
pistas: eight years · his manager
he wrote an email · a draft
on Monday · a meeting · his name appeared

historias.trap: 'Would have felt' es el condicional del pasado: para lo que habría pasado y no pasó.

historias.title: The House That Was Never Finished
historias.titleEs: La casa que nunca se terminó
text: On the road to my grandmother's town there is a house with no roof.
It was started in nineteen ninety-eight and it has never been finished.
People say the owner went abroad and never came back.
Every few years someone buys the land and plans to finish it.
Then nothing happens and the house stays exactly as it is.
Children in the town have invented three different stories about it.
My grandmother says the truth is much less interesting than any of them.

preguntas.q: What is missing from the house?
What do people say about the owner?
options: He went abroad and never returned
preguntas.answer: He went abroad and never returned

preguntas.q: What does the grandmother think?
options: The real story is less interesting
preguntas.answer: The real story is less interesting

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia de la casa como si se la contaras a alguien del pueblo.
pistas: a house with no roof · 1998
the owner · abroad
people buy it · nothing happens

historias.trap: 'It has never been finished' es pasiva en present perfect: has been + participio. El español lo diría con 'se': 'nunca se terminó'.

historias.title: Three Minutes Late
text: Laura had an interview at ten and she arrived three minutes after ten.
She apologized twice before she even sat down.
The interviewer told her that the previous candidate had not arrived at all.
The interview went well and she got the job.
Two years later she was the one doing the interviews.
Whenever someone arrives a few minutes late and apologizes too much, she remembers that morning.
She has never rejected anyone for being three minutes late.

preguntas.q: Why did Laura apologize?
What had happened with the previous candidate?
options: They had not come at all
preguntas.answer: They had not come at all

preguntas.q: What does Laura do now?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia de Laura desde la entrevista hasta hoy.
pistas: an interview at ten · 10:03
the previous candidate · had not arrived
two years later · she interviews

historias.trap: 'Had not arrived' es pasado perfecto: lo que pasó ANTES de otro momento pasado.

historias.title: What the Neighbours Heard
text: At two in the morning the whole building woke up.
Someone was playing the piano, badly but with enthusiasm.
By three o'clock four neighbors were standing in the hallway in pajamas.
Nobody wanted to be the one to knock.
Finally the oldest woman in the building went and knocked.
A boy of about nineteen opened the door and burst into tears.
He had failed an exam and it was the only thing that calmed him down.
The next night nobody complained.

preguntas.q: What woke the building up?
Who finally knocked on the door?
Why was the boy playing?
options: He was practicing for a concert

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta lo que pasó esa noche en el edificio.
pistas: two in the morning · the piano
four neighbors · the hallway
the oldest woman · a boy of nineteen

historias.trap: 'Burst into tears' = echarse a llorar. Es una frase hecha: no se traduce pieza por pieza.

historias.title: The Translation
text: A small museum asked my cousin to translate its signs into English.
She isn't a translator, but she speaks English well and they paid in cash.
She finished the job in two evenings and forgot about it.
Six months later a British tourist wrote a review online.
He said the museum was lovely but the English was full of mistakes.
My cousin read the review and recognized every single error he listed.
She now says that speaking a language and writing it professionally are two very different things.

preguntas.q: What is true about the cousin?
options: She speaks English well but isn't a translator
preguntas.answer: She speaks English well but isn't a translator

preguntas.q: What did the tourist say?
options: The English was full of mistakes
preguntas.answer: The English was full of mistakes

preguntas.q: What did she learn?
options: Speaking and writing professionally are different
preguntas.answer: Speaking and writing professionally are different

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta qué le pasó a tu prima y qué aprendió.
pistas: a small museum · the signs
six months later · a review
she recognized every error

historias.trap: 'Recognized every single error': 'single' refuerza, no significa soltero. 'Every single' = cada uno sin excepción.

historias.title: The Shortcut
text: My father drove the same route to work for twenty years.
One day a colleague told him about a shortcut that saved ten minutes.
He tried it once and got lost for half an hour.
He never used it again and told the story for years afterwards.
When I started driving, he gave me a serious warning about that road.
Last month I finally tried it out of curiosity.
It saves eleven minutes and it is impossible to get lost.
I have decided not to tell him.

preguntas.q: What did the colleague suggest?
What happened the first time?
What did the narrator discover?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia del atajo, la versión de tu padre y la tuya.
pistas: the same route · twenty years
a shortcut · he got lost
last month · it saves eleven minutes · I won't tell him

historias.trap: 'Afterwards' = después, sin decir de qué. 'After' necesita complemento: 'after the trip'. 'Afterwards' va solo: 'he told the story for years afterwards'.

historias.title: The Numbers That Didn't Add Up
text: Lucia had been analyzing the same data set for almost two years when she noticed something strange.
Several results from her supervisor's most famous paper could not be reproduced, no matter what she tried.
Having checked everything three times, she finally found the problem: a column had been copied twice by mistake.
When she showed him the error, her supervisor said it was minor and asked her to keep it quiet.
He reminded her that her scholarship depended on his funding and that her defense was only six months away.
If she had noticed the mistake a year earlier, she would be in a much stronger position now.
For two weeks she barely slept, writing and deleting the same email to the ethics committee again and again.
In the end, she sent it on a Monday morning, before she had time to change her mind.
The paper was withdrawn in March, and her supervisor stopped answering her messages.
Last week a student from another university thanked her; he had been about to build his whole thesis on those numbers.

preguntas.q: What was wrong with the data?
options: A column had been copied twice
preguntas.answer: A column had been copied twice

preguntas.q: What did her supervisor ask her to do?
Why was the student from another university grateful?
options: He almost used the wrong numbers in his thesis
Lucia had helped him get a scholarship
He had found the same mistake first
preguntas.answer: He almost used the wrong numbers in his thesis

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado; usa 'had been analyzing' (past perfect continuous) y la pasiva ('was withdrawn').
pistas: two years · something strange · a column copied twice
her supervisor · keep it quiet · her scholarship
the ethics committee · withdrawn · a student thanked her

historias.trap: 'Had been analyzing' dice cuánto llevaba haciendo algo cuando pasó otra cosa; no digas 'she was analyzing since two years'.

historias.title: The Counteroffer
text: Mateo had been working as an engineer at a small firm in Bogota for six years without a single raise.
When a company in Denver offered him a job, he was told that he had only a week to decide.
He mentioned the offer to his boss, expecting nothing more than polite congratulations and a farewell lunch.
Instead, she asked him to wait, and the next morning he was offered a salary almost twice as high.
She also promised that the company would finally pay for the English course he had been requesting for years.
Flattered and confused, Mateo spent the whole weekend making lists of reasons to stay and reasons to leave.
His wife said that if they really valued him, they would have paid him properly a long time ago.
His mother, on the other hand, told him that a bird in the hand was worth two in Denver.
He accepted the counteroffer, and for eight months everything seemed absolutely perfect.
Then the firm was sold, and the first job the new owners decided to cut was his.

preguntas.q: How long had Mateo been working without a raise?
What did his wife think?
options: The company should have paid him better before
He should move to Denver immediately
preguntas.answer: The company should have paid him better before

preguntas.q: What happened after the firm was sold?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado y reporta en estilo indirecto lo que dijeron su jefa, su esposa y su mamá ('she said that...').
pistas: six years · no raise · an offer in Denver
his boss · twice as high · the English course
his wife · his mother · the firm was sold

historias.trap: En estilo indirecto 'will' pasa a 'would': 'she promised the company would pay', no 'will pay'. Y aumento de sueldo es 'raise', no 'rise'.

historias.title: The Wrong Portland
text: Having booked the cheapest flight she could find, Valeria felt very proud of herself until the plane landed.
She had been planning the trip to visit her cousin in Portland, Oregon, for almost four months.
The airport, however, was in Portland, Maine, nearly three thousand miles away on the other side of the country.
At the information desk, she was told that this happened more often than most people would like to admit.
Her cousin laughed so hard on the phone that she had to hang up and call back later.
If Valeria had read the confirmation email carefully, she would have been eating salmon in Oregon that night.
Instead, she was sitting in a small hotel by the ocean, eating lobster and wondering what to do next.
The next morning, a woman she had met at breakfast offered her a ride along the coast.
They spent three days visiting lighthouses and talking about everything from divorce to their favorite recipes.
Valeria never made it to Oregon that year, but she has been back to Maine twice since then.

preguntas.q: Where did Valeria want to go?
Why did the mistake happen?
options: She did not read the confirmation carefully
Her cousin gave her the wrong city
preguntas.answer: She did not read the confirmation carefully

preguntas.q: What shows that the mistake turned out well?
options: She has returned to Maine twice
She got all her money back
preguntas.answer: She has returned to Maine twice

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta el viaje en pasado e incluye una frase con condicional en pasado ('If she had read..., she would have been...').
pistas: the cheapest flight · her cousin · Portland, Oregon
Portland, Maine · the information desk · her cousin laughed
a woman at breakfast · lighthouses · back twice

historias.trap: 'Offer someone a ride' es ofrecer llevarlo en carro; 'carry' es cargar algo o a alguien en los brazos.

historias.title: The Family Meeting
text: After their mother had fallen twice in one month, the three siblings were called to a family meeting.
Rosa, the oldest, had been visiting her every weekend and felt it was time for someone else to help.
Her brother suggested a nursing home, arguing that professionals would take better care of her than any of them.
Her sister, who lived abroad, offered to pay for everything but said she could not possibly move back.
Nobody had asked their mother what she wanted, which, looking back, was the strangest part of the evening.
When they finally did, she calmly announced that she had already made her own arrangements.
She had been secretly talking to her neighbor, a widower, who was also tired of living alone.
They had decided to share his ground-floor apartment and hire a nurse to come three times a week.
Her children were shocked, and her son asked whether this arrangement was even legal.
Their mother replied that she was eighty-one, not dead, and poured everyone another cup of coffee.

preguntas.q: Why was the family meeting called?
What did the brother suggest?
Who had their mother been talking to?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado y reporta en estilo indirecto lo que propuso cada hijo y lo que respondió la mamá.
pistas: fallen twice · a family meeting · Rosa
a nursing home · her sister abroad · nobody asked her
her neighbor · share his apartment · eighty-one, not dead

historias.trap: 'Siblings' incluye hermanos y hermanas; 'brothers' son solo hombres. 'Widower' es viudo y 'widow', viuda.

historias.title: The Report Nobody Read
text: For months, Diego's team had been using an AI tool to write the monthly reports for their clients.
The reports were generated in minutes, signed off by one of the team, and sent out without anyone reading them closely.
One morning a client called, furious, asking why his company had been described as a small bakery in Ohio.
His company was, in fact, a large logistics firm that had never sold a single loaf of bread.
Diego was asked to explain how such an obvious error had gotten through three levels of review.
Looking at the file, he realized that he himself had approved it on a busy Friday afternoon.
He could easily have blamed the software, and his manager seemed to be hoping that he would.
Instead, he admitted that he had signed a document he had not read and apologized to the client personally.
The client was surprisingly calm and said that honesty was rarer than good software these days.
Diego kept the account, but he still wonders whether he would have confessed if nobody had been watching.

preguntas.q: What was wrong with the report?
options: It described the client as a bakery
It was sent a month late
preguntas.answer: It described the client as a bakery

preguntas.q: Who had approved the report?
What does Diego still ask himself?
options: Whether he would have told the truth without witnesses
Whether he should stop using AI
preguntas.answer: Whether he would have told the truth without witnesses

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta la historia en pasado y usa la voz pasiva al menos dos veces ('the reports were checked', 'he was asked').
pistas: an AI tool · the monthly reports
a furious client · a small bakery · three levels of review
he had approved it · he apologized · he still wonders

historias.trap: 'Blame' va sin 'to': 'blame the software (for the error)'. 'Apologize' lleva 'to' para la persona y 'for' para la falta: 'apologize to the client for the error'.

historias.title: The Tree Between Two Houses
text: The old oak tree had been growing between the two houses long before either family moved in.
Every fall its leaves blocked the gutters next door, and every fall the neighbor, Mr. Harris, complained to Carolina.
This year he sent her a letter from a lawyer, claiming that the tree was damaging his roof.
Carolina, having grown up with that tree, refused to even consider cutting it down.
A surveyor was hired to settle the question of whose property the tree was actually on.
The result surprised everyone: the trunk stood almost entirely on his side of the line.
Legally, the tree belonged to him, and so, she was told, did the decision.
Carolina expected to hear a chainsaw the following morning, but nothing happened for weeks.
Then a note appeared under her door saying that he had cleaned his gutters and would keep the tree.
She still does not know whether he had changed his mind or had simply been enjoying the fight.

preguntas.q: What did the lawyer's letter claim?
options: The tree was damaging the roof
The tree was blocking the view
preguntas.answer: The tree was damaging the roof

preguntas.q: What did the surveyor discover?
options: The tree was on the neighbor's side
The tree was on Carolina's side
The tree was exactly on the line
preguntas.answer: The tree was on the neighbor's side

preguntas.q: What did the neighbor finally decide?

retell.prompt_es: Cuenta el conflicto en pasado y termina con tu opinión: ¿por qué crees que el vecino cambió de idea?
pistas: an old oak tree · the gutters · Mr. Harris complained
a lawyer · a surveyor · his side of the line
a note · keep the tree · enjoying the fight

historias.trap: 'Whose' pregunta de quién es algo ('whose property'); suena igual que 'who's' (who is), pero no es lo mismo.
